label: OVERVIEW
title: Two interfaces. One source of truth.
narration: Intent QA separates the application under test from the evidence workspace. The shop runs locally, while this dashboard reads the same file-backed QA artifacts used by the command line and the native agent.

label: SEMANTIC TEST
title: Human-readable YAML, validated before save
narration: Tests stay human-readable. This YAML records intent and observable outcomes, never selectors or coordinates. The editor reuses the authoritative validator, preserves the document identity, and saves atomically only after references are valid.

label: SCENARIO 1 · PASS
title: Reusable login fixture
narration: First, the stable journey. A reusable login fixture signs in without exposing credentials in evidence. The agent reaches the customer dashboard and begins the unchanged checkout specification.

label: SCENARIO 1 · PASS
title: Semantic navigation
narration: The agent opens the shopping cart and checks the visible outcome: exactly one item is present. It resolves the checkout action semantically instead of relying on a stored selector.

label: SCENARIO 1 · PASS
title: Expectations remain explicit
narration: At checkout, the next expectation is visible before submission. The saved test card and total are present, so the agent performs the approved payment action and continues.

label: SCENARIO 1 · PASS
title: Approved outcome observed
narration: The expected confirmation appears with no error message. Cleanup runs afterward, screenshots are stored, and the functional result is classified as passed.

label: RESULT · PASSED
title: Steps, targets, and evidence
narration: The result view explains the decision. Every step passed, every original expectation is preserved, and each selected accessible target is recorded beside the evidence captured during the run.

label: SCENARIO 2 · HARMLESS DRIFT
title: The control moved and changed name
narration: Now the demo resets to harmless drift. Proceed to checkout has moved inside a menu and is renamed Continue to payment. The specification and its expected checkout form remain unchanged.

label: RESULT · HEALED
title: Equivalent target, unchanged expectation
narration: The original target is absent, so the agent captures the failure, rediscovers an explicitly equivalent accessible control, retries once, and verifies the same expectation. Before-and-after evidence supports the healed classification.

label: SCENARIO 3 · REAL BUG
title: Interaction succeeds; outcome fails
narration: Next is a genuine functional bug. The checkout interaction still succeeds, but the application shows an order failure instead of the required confirmation. This is not eligible for healing.

label: RESULT · FUNCTIONAL REGRESSION
title: No assertion rewriting
narration: The result stays honest: functional regression. The missing confirmation is recorded as the failed observable outcome, later steps do not invent success, and the original assertion is never rewritten.

label: SCENARIO 4 · DESIGN MISMATCH
title: Functionally correct, visibly wrong
narration: Finally, the behavior works, but the approved confirmation design does not. The action moves ahead of the heading, and the green success treatment becomes a prominent red warning panel.

label: RESULT · DESIGN REGRESSION
title: Reference-backed visual findings
narration: Because the functional steps passed, the explicit design checkpoint runs at its declared viewport. Concrete order and style findings, plus the actual screenshot and reference provenance, support a design regression.

label: COMPLETE MVP
title: Intent survives drift. Regressions stay visible.
narration: That is the complete loop: semantic YAML, reusable fixtures, native execution, conservative healing, functional and design classification, and inspectable file-backed evidence. Harmless drift recovers; real regressions remain visible.
